Good evening, passengers on SkyAmerica Flight nine fifty-one to São Paulo. Because of the snowstorm, there is a ground stop for all departures from JFK, and this flight is now canceled. We are very sorry, but the weather is beyond our control. All passengers have been rebooked on tomorrow's flight at nine fifteen p.m. If you need an earlier flight, please ask an agent at gate twelve to put you on the waitlist for the morning flight at eight oh five. Because this cancellation is caused by weather, we are not able to offer hotel rooms tonight. However, if you choose not to travel, you are entitled to a full refund. Please check your email for all the details.

Last winter, a client called me from the airport in Chicago. Her flight was canceled, she was stranded, and she slept on the floor of the terminal. If she had called me first, I would have found her a hotel room in ten minutes. Here are three lessons from that night. First, don't just wait in the long line at the desk. While you wait, call the airline or use the app. The phone is often faster than the line. Second, keep every receipt: the taxi, the hotel, and the food. Without receipts, you can't file a claim for a reimbursement. Third, read the fine print before you travel. It tells you what you are entitled to. And remember: the agent at the desk didn't cause the snow. Be kind, and people will help you more.

First, I read the email from the airline and check the reason for the cancellation. Then, I call the airline while I wait in the line at the desk. Next, I ask the agent to put me on the waitlist for an earlier flight. After that, I book a hotel near the airport and keep every receipt. Finally, I file a claim online for a reimbursement.
